sections.title: Server Responses
sections.note: Tag identity, untagged data and continuation framing have component proofs; unsolicited update/client memory duties remain separate.

sections.title: Server Responses - Status Responses
sections.note: Each named response code is dispositioned below. Optional availability and client presentation/unknown-code duties do not imply server implementation.

sections.title: OK Response
sections.note: OK greeting begins unauthenticated; tagged OK marks success. Optional informational alerts are not emitted.

sections.title: NO Response
sections.note: Tagged NO reports operational failure while selection remains usable. Optional untagged warnings are not emitted.

sections.title: BAD Response
sections.note: Undetermined commands, including blank lines, receive untagged BAD. Determined protocol failures carry their own tag; the next command remains usable.

sections.title: PREAUTH Response
sections.note: PREAUTH is not offered. Its protected-transport recommendation and client refusal duty do not establish a server feature.

sections.title: BYE Response
sections.note: LOGOUT sends BYE then tagged OK; panic, deadline and refusal paths close after untagged BYE. Deadline injection proves handling, not elapsed production timing.

sections.title: Server Responses - Server and Mailbox Status
sections.note: Server and mailbox status data are untagged; completion is separate.

sections.title: CAPABILITY Response
sections.note: Rev1 capability baseline and protected-authentication advertisement have proofs; unknown-capability tolerance is client-side.

sections.title: LIST Response
sections.note: LIST syntax, attributes, separator consistency and reusable mailbox names have narrow component proofs; arbitrary hidden-child ACLs remain host-side.

sections.title: LSUB Response
sections.note: LSUB has its own response name; separate subscription persistence remains the recorded backend boundary.

sections.title: STATUS Response
sections.note: STATUS names the requested mailbox and attributes; detailed item/backend identity boundaries remain in the STATUS family.

sections.title: SEARCH Response
sections.note: SEARCH sequence/UID results have existing component proofs. The complete response example is not a new transcript claim.

sections.title: FLAGS Response
sections.note: FLAGS and PERMANENTFLAGS have distinct scopes; keyword persistence and client memory duties remain separate.

sections.title: Server Responses - Mailbox Size
sections.note: Numeric mailbox counts are untagged; RECENT remains an explicit approximation.

sections.title: EXISTS Response
sections.note: EXISTS reports total messages on selection and updates. Remembering the new count is a client duty.

sections.title: RECENT Response
sections.note: True Recent ownership is not implemented; unseen-count approximation must not be presented as conformance.

sections.title: Server Responses - Message Status
sections.note: Message data use sequence-number prefixes; full FETCH structure semantics remain in the component families.

sections.title: EXPUNGE Response
sections.note: Sequence renumbering and EXPUNGE restrictions are separate. UID commands MAY expunge; current deferral is a narrower valid choice.

sections.title: FETCH Response
sections.note: Metadata, body structures, sections and partials have narrower proofs. Host wire representation and all grammar alternatives remain explicit limits.

sections.title: Server Responses - Command Continuation Request
sections.note: Continuation requests precede synchronizing payloads and SASL challenges. Client wait-before-send duty is distinct from server framing.

sections.title: ENABLED Response
sections.note: ENABLED lists successfully enabled features, including empty results. This does not imply ENABLE IMAP4rev2.

sections.note: Mailbox status data remain untagged.

sections.title: LIST Response

sections.title: NAMESPACE Response
sections.note: Personal namespace and NIL unavailable namespace classes are offered; shared/other-user namespaces and arbitrary ACLs are not inferred.

sections.title: STATUS Response

sections.title: ESEARCH Response
sections.note: ESEARCH item uniqueness, empty-result omissions, matching sets and COUNT have component proofs. Rev2 default SEARCH switching is not implemented.

sections.title: FLAGS Response

sections.title: Server Responses - Mailbox Size
sections.note: Numeric mailbox totals remain untagged; rev2 removes RECENT rather than proving the rev1 approximation.

sections.title: Server Responses - Message Status
sections.note: Message data use sequence-number prefixes; full FETCH structure semantics remain in the component families.

sections.title: EXPUNGE Response
sections.note: Sequence renumbering and incomplete-command restrictions are separate. UID commands MAY expunge; current deferral is stricter, not a normative UID prohibition.

sections.title: FETCH Response
sections.note: BINARY representation, sizes and refusal paths, partial origins and ordered structures are separate. Text canonicalization, host BODY encoding and unsolicited UID formatting remain recorded rev2 boundaries.
